description: TM-D710A clone-mode programming (256-byte R/W blocks after 0M PROGRAM; skips radio block 0x7F)

aprs.help: Control-head COM jack, not the body PC memory or CAT port. Match menu 528 to this baud. HamBench does not change radio menus.
aprs.monitorNote: Passive monitor only. Menu 604 OUTPUT ON copies heard APRS while the radio is showing APRS. COM baud is menu 528. HamBench does not change that menu.

host.flowHelp: Software is the default and keeps RTS and DTR low, as does Off. Hardware (RTS/CTS) is required when the TNC already shows XFLOW OFF. The driver handles RTS. It does not force RTS low and it does not send XFLOW.
setup: Connect listens, then enters KISS on its own. Command text such as cmd: runs KISS ON, then RESTART after another cmd:. Silence sends three Ctrl+C once. If it is still silent, Connect sends the KISS exit frame once and waits for cmd:. It stops if that stays silent. Connect does not transmit RF: no beacon, HB, RESET, XFLOW, or KISS OFF.

Head COM is not the CAT or memory port. Menu 528 is the COM baud. The tested host path is menu 529 PACKET data band B on 144.390. Menu 604 OUTPUT is the passive monitor only. HamBench does not change those menus.
recovery: On this radio KISS did not persist across a power cycle. After the radio was off overnight on 11 Nov 2026, the TNC came up in command mode, emitted TNC2 monitor text and cmd:, and replied KISS was OFF.

kissExit is the KISS specification return-from-KISS frame C0 FF C0. The Kenwood manuals have not verified that frame on the TM-D710. It is not a manual-verified exit. The A/E KISS sentence says power OFF then ON causes the TNC to enter (or exit) KISS when the parameter is ON. The G sentence uses RESTART for that wording. Neither says the result alternates. A startup banner is not proof of PACKET mode.
